visualReview.notes: Inspected the lit site preview, four turntables and close views of the main hall, Buddhaisawan Chapel, Red House and linked Phra Wiman roofs. The street view shows the hall’s stepped tile roof and porch. The chapel stair, gold surrounds and limestone foundations are visible. The Red House now reads as timber carried above ground on posts.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected nine dated geographic viewer frames. The mapped palace complex loaded and unloaded with lime plaster, tile, stone, timber and paving. In the overhead view both Phra Wiman court openings and the sixteen envelopes remain distinct.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 current images. The four detail levels and their transitions all retain the compound layout, chapel, main hall, raised Red House and the Phra Wiman voids. Near levels add gable relief, finials, tile bands, porch posts and stairs.

geographicReview.notes: The OSM museum relation selects the compound and each building envelope; the Phra Wiman multipolygon supplies both courtyard openings. Reviewed the original unmasked source field and terrain-backed site shots. Coarse composite elevation obscures parts of some lower foundations and the exact historic finished grade is approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Bangkok National Museum’s Front Palace complex in its 2017 appearance, including Siwamokkhaphiman Hall, Buddhaisawan Chapel, the Issarawinitchai and Phra Wiman range, the Red House, Royal Chariot Hangar and associated exhibition halls.
fidelityReview.notes: Thai architectural documentation supplies the long stepped temple roofs, hall bays, chapel terraces, square columns, and the three connected residential roofs. The exact cleared Qualla hall original and the two licensed portal originals inform the deep window openings, red-brown beams, gilded entrances and steps. Roof pitches, trim relief, detailed room subdivision and associated museum façades are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: The single exact Qualla image and two supplementary original-upload photographs have verified same-photographer CC0 dedications and matching native hashes. The circa-1890 photograph was excluded. The geometry uses shared procedural material graphs and authored colors.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Bangkok National Museum and the surviving Front Palace structures in their 2017 appearance, including Siwamokkhaphiman, Buddhaisawan, Issarawinitchai and Phra Wiman, the Red House and later museums.

limitations: The native map defines each building footprint and the two Phra Wiman courtyard openings. Roof pitch, wall section, distribution of doors and windows, and heights of associated museum buildings are architectural estimates.

Three exact 2017 reference images support the entrances and hall finishes. Written Thai architectural records supply the building types, ceremonial roof forms and relationships elsewhere in the compound.
Gilt reliefs, roof finials and fretwork are simplified. The depicted carvings, murals, Buddhist images and portable collections are outside the modeled scope.
The original elevation samples include effects from trees, roofs and the nearby river. Finished paving, stairs and exact historical foundation heights are approximate.
